page: Microsoft Azure E248ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv7 series, operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 248 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 1888.0 GB of system memory. This configuration achieves an allocation ratio of approximately 7.61 GB of RAM per vCPU, targeting workloads that require significant memory footprints combined with substantial multi-threaded processing power.

Storage capability on the E248ds_v7 includes 15118 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage, offering significant local capacity for scratch space, temporary indexing, and caching. The server is also capable of interfacing with Premium Storage for remote persistent volumes. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators, directing all platform resources toward host-level compute execution, memory operations, and local NVMe storage throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E248ds_v7 functions as an enterprise resource consolidation platform. Provisioning 248 dedicated processor cores alongside nearly 1.9 TB of RAM within a single virtual instance minimizes the inter-node networking overhead often seen in distributed clusters. Realizing economic value from this configuration depends on continuous saturation of both its dense memory array and its extensive core count.

The platform is suited for memory-bound and data-dense enterprise workloads. Primary use cases include massive in-memory databases, large enterprise relational database management systems, large-scale extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines, enterprise resource planning (ERP) deployments, and memory-resident data analytics engines.
